meta.title: Two Animals in the Nature Park

paragraphs: Animal File by Mia. This is my animal file for Explorers' Blog. Last Saturday, the Explorers visited the nature park with Ranger Mark. We walked for one hour on a path under the tall trees. He told us about two wild animals that live there. Teacher Kim read my file before it went online.

Beetles. A beetle is an insect with a hard back. Like every insect, a beetle has six legs. Under the hard back, it has two thin wings. Many beetles can fly, but you cannot always see their wings. If a beetle falls on its back, it turns over with its legs. Ranger Mark showed us a green beetle on a leaf. It was smaller than my finger. Some beetles are black, and some are bright red or green.

Eagles. An eagle is a big bird with strong wings. It builds a nest in a tall tree. Its feet are strong, and it holds its food with them. Ranger Mark believes that two eagles live on the hill behind the park. We did not see them, but we saw a large nest in a tree. An eagle can see a small animal from far away. A young eagle stays in the nest for many weeks. The parents bring food to it every day. If the wind is strong, it flies high without a move of its wings.

The Future. Many wild animals lose a part of their home every year. When people cut the trees, the beetles and the birds have nowhere to go. Ranger Mark says, "A clean forest has a good future for them." If we keep the park clean, the animals stay. We can all help. Put your bottles in a bin. Do not pick the flowers, and do not go near a nest. Which animal do you like best? Tell us in a message under this post!
